blocks.x: The working definition of Generative AI Platform Engineering at Dataq Software: scope we sign, the cadence you can plan around, platform evidence generated in-flight, and outcomes measured against your baseline.

Enterprises that build GenAI apps ad hoc end up with a dozen disconnected stacks, inconsistent guardrails and no idea what inference costs. We build the alternative: a central GenAI platform providing model routing, managed retrieval, prompt and policy management, evaluation applies, red-teaming hooks, and per-team cost meters — so product teams ship in days on rails that risk teams already trust.

The platform is model-agnostic by design: frontier APIs, open-weight models served on vLLM, and fine-tuned specialists behind one gateway with semantic caching, fallback routing and PII redaction enforced at the edge. Every response carries provenance metadata, so audit can trace an answer to the document, the model version and the policy that allowed it.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
